summary: Nothing that waits on you is forgotten, and you can see and revoke privileged access on a visual map.

new.title: A reminder when something waits on you
new.text: SuperAdmins get one reminder mail listing everything waiting on them, each with a link. Change it under Settings > Mail & alerting > Reminders: what waits on you.

new.title: Delegation overview with a graph view
new.text: All privileged permissions now shows live access as a map of people, groups, roles and scopes. Click a path, tick what to take away and press Revoke.

new.title: Setup needs no extra tools
new.text: Setup and support scripts no longer need the Azure CLI or PowerShell modules, and the PIM Manager image is slimmer.

new.title: Your DNS stays yours
new.text: With a custom host name, setup no longer changes your Active Directory DNS. It prints the one record to add and a command to check it.

fixes.title: Access reviews also ask department owners
fixes.text: Department owners now always review their department; extra reviewers on a review rule join them instead of replacing them.
fixes.action: To keep the old behaviour, tick "only these reviewers (not the owners)" on the review rule.

fixes.title: Drift Apply now applies only what you ticked
fixes.text: Before, Apply now re-applied every missing and changed item. Now only the items you ticked are created or updated.

fixes.title: Mail recipients get working Reader access
fixes.text: Recipients whose mail address differs from their sign-in name now get Reader access under the name they sign in with.

fixes.title: Old workload rows no longer block commits
fixes.text: An old workload row without a Resource now shows as a warning instead of blocking your commits.

fixes.title: Smaller fixes
fixes.text: New mail layout for alerts, auto-extend moved to Settings > Automation, a clear loading message on delegations, readable list columns and clearer revoke wording.
